title: Which Merchant Credits Are Set Off Against a Temporary Dispute Credit
content:
Merchant credits the cardholder has already received are set off against the temporary credit on a card under Personal Credit Cards, and which of them count is read from the cardholder's holdings under Savings & Money Market Accounts.

| What the savings records show | Merchant credits set off |
|---|---|
| An active savings account whose balance is at least 25000.00 USD, and at least 1 savings withdrawal posted to the cardholder's savings accounts in the last three months | every merchant credit posted to the card account in the last six months |
| An active savings account whose balance is below 25000.00 USD, and at least 1 savings withdrawal posted to the cardholder's savings accounts in the last three months | only the most recent merchant credit posted to the card account |
| Neither of those | no merchant credit is set off |

**Both parts together.** Each of the first two rows requires an active savings account of the stated balance and at least 1 savings withdrawal in the last three months. A cardholder with an active savings balance of 60000.00 USD and no savings withdrawal in that window falls in the third row.

**What the difference is worth.** On a card account carrying merchant credits of 30.00 USD, 12.00 USD and 8.00 USD posted in the last six months, the most recent of them being 8.00 USD, the first row sets off 50.00 USD, the second sets off 8.00 USD and the third sets off nothing. A balance of exactly 25000.00 USD belongs to the first row, the test being at least that amount, and 24999.99 USD to the second.
